material_definitions: The spinel-type solid solutions Li(4-2x)MgxTi(5-x)/3O4 were investigated for their ionic conductivity.
Samples were prepared via a solid-state reaction method using Li2CO3, MgO, and TiO2 as precursors.
The mixtures were calcined in air at 900 °C for 24 hours.
Ionic conductivity measurements were performed using an AC impedance technique in the temperature range from 25 to 300 °C.

material_definitions: A systematic study of Li1+xMxTi2-x(PO4)3 with M=Al, Cr and Fe and 0 <= x <= 1 has been carried out.
The addition of trivalent metals into the LiTi2(PO4)3 compound gives rise to the liberation of the M1 sites and simultaneous occupation of the M2' sites.
Both dc bulk and grain boundary ionic conductivity show a thermally activated behavior, and their values increase with substituent content until compositions of x = 0.2-0.3.
The activation energy for bulk dc conductivity hardly changes with the substitution, and the main factor affecting the variation of the ionic conductivity is the pre-exponential factor.
warnings: Temperature 'room temperature' was interpreted as 25 Celsius.

material_definitions: The samples belong to the series Li1+xMxTi2-x(PO4)3 where M represents Al, Fe, or Cr.
Ionic transport and charge dynamics were investigated using complex impedance spectroscopy across wide frequency and temperature ranges.
Bulk and grain boundary conductivity components were separated using combined conductivity and electrical modulus representations.
Neutron powder diffraction (NPD) was used to analyze the crystal structure and site occupancy of lithium ions (M1 and M2' sites).
Sample density was found to increase with substitution level, ranging from 45% to 70% of theoretical density.
warnings: The temperature was specified as 'room temperature'; 25°C is used as a standard numeric representation.
This value corresponds to the grain boundary conductivity (sigma^gb).
